route_file_rest_import_allowlist.allowed_usage: NIP-98-signed REST publish mutation only; Config Fabric reads derive from verified store events.
NIP-98-signed maintenance mutation only; health reads derive from verified store events.

entries.surface: Dashboard `/` and shared dashboard stores
evidence: Shared dashboard loaders call bootstrapControlplane().
Read-model bootstrap subscribes to scoped filters, tracks EOSE, and keeps subscriptions open for realtime updates.

entries.surface: `/orgs/**` organization read models, membership, invites, and mutations
evidence: Org pages read org, org-member, and org-invite 30900 records from the local store via readConfidentialTopic(), decrypted with the per-org content key (OCK).

Org create/update/delete, membership, and invite operations are signed org-domain intents published through publishIntent; internal/adapters/nostr/org_canonical_publisher.go publishes the resulting canonical state.
The pages import no $lib/api REST client.

entries.surface: `/payments` private payment history
evidence: Payment history is read from OCK-encrypted payment-record 30900 cp-state in the local store (readConfidentialTopic).
The daemon publishes payment records through the payment canonical publisher; the page issues no REST or request/result calls.

entries.surface: `/notifications/**` channel config, tests, and logs
evidence: Channel configuration and delivery logs are read from OCK-encrypted notification-channel and notification-log 30900 cp-state in the local store.
Channel create/update/delete and test operations are signed notification-domain intents (submitSensitiveIntent); delivery may target Nostr DMs.

entries.surface: `/services/**` current web route read models and public commands
evidence: Service list/detail pages use relay-backed stores and signed service-domain intent helpers.
REST service endpoints are compatibility surfaces; the routes do not use them for command ingress.

entries.surface: `/environments/**` route read models and public commands
evidence: Environment routes read via Nostr stores and create/update/delete through signed environment-domain 30900 intents with OK/result/projection trace coverage in web/tests/e2e/environments-crud-smoke.spec.js.
Detail route waits for explicit Nostr result events for worker policy changes and hydrates environment/state/history rows from canonical 30900 read models.

entries.surface: `/deployments/**` route read models, commands, and private log snapshots
evidence: Deployment routes use Nostr stores and public-controlplane actions.
Run logs are presented as public relay projection plus encrypted Nostr request/result fetch.

entries.surface: `/artifacts/**` registry artifacts and Nostr signature verification
evidence: Artifact registry data is loaded from Nostr-backed stores.
Artifact signature verification uses encrypted Nostr verification UI/store paths and does not use direct REST mutation.
The Builds page uses signed ContextVM build/result commands and canonical build/artifact projections.

entries.surface: Artifact Blossom controls and SBOM/attestation details
evidence: Blossom list/server/health calls use HTTP endpoints, which is expected for Blossom storage surfaces.
Artifact detail SBOM and attestation calls use REST API client methods.

entries.surface: `/packages/**` package read models and promote/yank commands
evidence: Package loaders use Nostr-backed stores.
Detail actions use public control-plane Nostr command helpers.

entries.surface: `/policies/**` current route read models and commands
evidence: Policy routes import Nostr stores and signed policy-domain intent helpers.
The daemon mounts no policy REST mutation routes; signer-first Nostr policy intents are the supported path.

entries.surface: `/config-fabric/**` desired/effective configuration, audit, publish, and rollback
evidence: The browser consumes desired and config-status Nostr events through the Config Fabric drift API.
Publish and rollback requests are validated, signed by the configured operator Signet identity, persisted as desired events, and require relay acceptance.
The browser never receives or submits a raw signing key and rejects secret-looking policy content before publication.

entries.surface: `/workers/**` worker ads, status, and control commands
evidence: Worker pages load worker Nostr stores and publish signed Nostr commands.
REST worker reads are compatibility/catalog endpoints; the routes do not use them for command ingress.

entries.surface: `/fleet-health` worker pressure and cleanup orchestration dashboard
evidence: Fleet Health reads worker, assignment, telemetry, and cleanup execution projections from shared Nostr-backed stores.
Cleanup actions are delegated to the worker cleanup request dialog rather than a route-level REST mutation.

entries.surface: `/instance-health` managed-runtime watchdog status, history, recovery attempts, and maintenance controls
evidence: The Instance Health page imports $lib/api/client.js for bounded health, event, recovery-attempt, and maintenance API calls.

Collection reads are organization-scoped in PostgreSQL through service and environment ownership joins; maintenance mutations require an authenticated service operator and invoke the local managed-instance supervisor.
Classified REST compatibility: the page publishes no browser-signed Nostr supervision commands.

entries.surface: `/adoption` runtime target scan and bounded status findings
evidence: Adoption scan publishes adoption/scan as a signed 30900 intent and renders findings from the matching 30315 status data; no ContextVM or REST request is issued.

entries.surface: `/ml` import and deployment browser submissions
evidence: ML page publishes ml/model-import, ml/recipe-apply, ml/recipe-run, ml/inference-deploy, ml/inference-approval, ml/inference-rollback, and ml/pin as signed 30900 intents through publishIntent().
Daemon status 30315 and canonical ML projections reconcile accepted work; no ML ContextVM request remains.
web/src/lib/api/client.js exposes no ML REST bridge methods or ML read-model facades.

entries.surface: `/ml` existing endpoint worker pin command
evidence: Existing endpoint pinning publishes an ml/pin signed intent with canonical endpoint revision before deployment submission.
The daemon updates the endpoint canonical placement policy; the browser does not issue a ContextVM pin command.

entries.surface: `/llm` route read models and operational mutations
evidence: LLM page imports public-controlplane actions and requester/kind helpers.
LLM operational mutations are signer-first Nostr kinds; the daemon mounts no LLM operational REST mutation routes.

entries.surface: `/dns` and FIPS DNS mesh
evidence: DNS store uses scoped Nostr read-model subscriptions with onEvent, onEose, onClosed, and onAuth callbacks.
DNS command helper publishes signed requests and awaits explicit Bahia result events.

entries.surface: `/backup/**` read models and public commands
evidence: Backup routes call relay-backed stores and public-controlplane actions for probe/approve/reject flows.

entries.surface: `/continuity` status, topology, and simulation
evidence: Continuity load calls loadContinuityDashboardFromNostr() and consumes scoped relay filters for kind 30351/30353 status plus 31400-31404 definitions and NIP-38 kind 30315 continuity heartbeat events scoped by #domain=continuity.

internal/kinds/policy.go classifies continuity heartbeat status 30315, continuity observables 30351-30353, and definitions 31400-31404 as canonical readable projection kinds; internal/relaysidecar/policy.go consumes that shared policy for sidecar REQ admission.
SimulationPanel derives worker-failure impact locally from the same Nostr event set instead of POSTing to a REST simulation endpoint.
The daemon serves no /api/continuity/status, /api/continuity/topology, or /api/continuity/simulate HTTP routes.

entries.surface: `/souls/**` Soul Factory pages and `/settings/fleet` OpenClaw fleet configuration
evidence: Soul routes use Nostr client/store helpers and direct subscriptions.
The fleet settings route subscribes to and publishes signed parameterized-replaceable kind 31953 events directly through the Nostr client.

entries.surface: `/events` relay activity route
evidence: Events route imports event/read-model stores and labels relay connection state.

entries.surface: `/widgets` trusted operations widget wall
evidence: Ops Widgets uses Bahia's recovering, signature-validating PoolBackedClient for kind 30318 and delegates event trust storage, envelope validation, templates, and fallbacks to Wheelhouse.

entries.surface: `/security` and `/security/[id]` SBOM/OSV scan findings and schedules
evidence: Security pages import the security store for finding/schedule list and rescan operations.
The security store uses HTTP-native API client calls for OSV/SBOM security surfaces rather than browser Nostr command ingress.

entries.surface: `/settings` discovery and local relay/signer configuration
evidence: Settings manipulates Nostr client relay configuration and Nostr Connect auth.
System discovery/bootstrap may be HTTP-native and is not treated as fake Nostr control-plane command ingress.

entries.surface: `/settings/profile` signer-backed Nostr profile metadata publishing
evidence: Profile settings builds standard kind-0 metadata events, signs through the active NIP-07 or NIP-46 auth signer flow, and publishes to writable signer/NIP-65 relays.
publishProfileMetadata() checks per-relay OK outcomes and requires at least one accepted=true relay before updating cached profile state.

entries.surface: `/settings/relays` operator relay policy, relay administration, and local browser relay reconnect controls
evidence: `/settings/relays` renders RelaySettingsPanel, which reads canonical 30900 relay-settings state via subscribeRelayPolicyReadModel() with #d/domain/schema filters plus EOSE/CLOSED/AUTH callbacks.
Relay policy and relay-admin operations are signed relay-domain intents (submitSensitiveIntent); local browser relay add/remove/reconnect is client-local Nostr relay configuration.

entries.surface: `/docs` and `/docs/[topic]` central documentation browser reads via NIP-23
evidence: Docs pages subscribe to kind 30023 (NIP-23 long-form content) events tagged with bahia-docs from the relay and treat EOSE as historical catch-up completion.
Backend NostrDocsPublisher syncs docs/user-guide/ Markdown to relay as addressable NIP-23 events on startup with content-hash change detection.
The docs route files import no REST API client and fetch no /api/v1/docs.

entries.surface: Standalone relay sidecar HTTP/NIP-11/WebSocket server on `/` or configured `/relay` path
evidence: cmd/relay/main.go starts relaysidecar.New(...).Run(ctx) when nostr.sidecar.enabled is true.

internal/relaysidecar/server.go creates a net/http server and serves the Khatru relay for NIP-11 HTTP metadata plus Nostr WebSocket traffic on `/` and the path from nostr.sidecar.public_url such as `/relay`.
This surface is Nostr relay infrastructure (NIP-11 HTTP metadata plus WebSocket), not REST CRUD.

entries.surface: Mounted `/api/v1` compatibility endpoints for non-browser clients and domain reads/writes
evidence: The router mounts REST compatibility routes for non-browser clients and domain surfaces outside browser command ingress (health/readiness, DB-less payment reads, and similar).
web/src/lib/api/client.js keeps only the HTTP-native Blossom/SBOM interop helpers used by web routes.

entries.surface: `/route-canaries` managed-route outage state, detail, and event lineage, plus the RouteCanaryOutages component embedded in the service and environment detail pages
evidence: The Route Canaries page imports $lib/api/client.js for bounded route canary list, detail, and event-lineage API calls.

Route canary state is also projected to signed Nostr observables (NIP-38 status, 30900 state, 4903 audit); this surface stays REST compatibility because the REST API is read-only and server-owned, serving bounded history, lineage, and per-route detail reads with no browser-signed command ingress.

web/src/lib/components/RouteCanaryOutages.svelte is the only place services/[id] and environments/[id] read this surface: it owns the REST call so those nostr_native pages never import $lib/api/client.js themselves. The component lives under web/src/lib and is registered here as control_files; it is read-only.
